issues.description: The problem statement's UML and task description indicate addGuestStudents(int) should be a void method (UML: +addGuestStudents(int): void; task: "Implement a addGuestStudents(int) method which adds a new number of guest students to the lecture"). The solution implementation provides addGuestStudents(int) with a boolean return type (returns true/false) instead of void. This creates a method return-type mismatch: students following the UML/text will implement a void method, but the solution/reference uses a boolean return value. This can confuse students about the expected signature and cause incompatibility with any tests or references that rely on the solution's signature.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution's addGuestStudents method signature match the problem specification/UML. Change the solution implementation to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { this.numberOfGuestStudents += numberOfNewGuestStudents; } (or, if a boolean return is intentional, update the problem statement and UML to indicate the method returns boolean and document the meaning of the return value).
